title: Problem: two sum (PHP) — hash map thinking

lesson.picture: You're looking for a dance partner whose height plus yours equals 340 cm. Instead of asking every pair (O(n²)), you write everyone's height on a board as they arrive and just check 'is 340 − mine on the board?' (O(n)).
lesson.concept:
Given an array and a target, return indices of two numbers that sum to target. Brute force is O(n²). The senior answer trades memory for time: one pass, keep a map value → index, and for each number check whether target − number is already in the map.

This pattern (lookup table for the complement) shows up everywhere: duplicate detection, pairing transactions, matching webhook events.
lesson.bn: প্রতিটা সংখ্যার জন্য দেখো target − সংখ্যা আগে দেখা হয়েছে কিনা (hash map-এ value → index)। এক pass, O(n) সময়, O(n) memory। Brute force O(n²)। 'complement খোঁজা' pattern-টা অনেক জায়গায় লাগে।

practice.task: Variation: return ALL pairs of indices whose values sum to target (values may repeat). Keep it O(n).
Explain in two sentences to a junior why the hash-map version is faster than two nested loops, using the 'dance partner' picture.
practice.solution:
```php
Nested loops ask every pair 'do you two add up?' — that's n×n questions. The map writes each height on a board as people arrive, so each new person asks one question: 'is my partner already on the board?' — n questions total.
```

cards.q: Two sum: brute force complexity vs optimal, and the trade-off
cards.a: O(n²) vs O(n) time; optimal uses O(n) extra memory for a value→index map.

cards.q: Why check the map before inserting the current number?
cards.a: So a number isn't paired with itself when target = 2 × number.

cards.q: Name another problem solved by the same 'lookup the complement' idea
cards.a: Detecting duplicate transactions / finding pairs with a given difference / matching webhook events to orders.
